courses.subject: CSS
courses.title: Introductory Programming for Computational Social Science
courses.description: This course develops computational thinking practices and skills critical for defining, describing, and analyzing social science problems using a computational approach. Students will learn to program in Python in the context of computational social science problems.

courses.subject: CSS
courses.title: Data and Model Programming for Computational Social Science
courses.description: This course explores the use of computational methods across the social sciences. Topics include thinking like a computational social scientist; research design for big data; legal and ethical dimensions of computational social science (CSS). Students will implement demonstrations of these methods in Python.
courses.prereqText: CSS 1 and choose one of the following courses: COGS 14B, MATH 11, MGT 3, POLI 30, POLI 30D, PSYC 60.

courses.subject: CSS
courses.title: Advanced Programming for Computational Social Science
courses.description: This course develops advanced computational problem-solving skills including common algorithms, data structures, and advanced tool and library options. The class provides further development in Python.

courses.subject: CSS
courses.title: Environmental Data Science
courses.description: This is an upper-division course focused on understanding some of the many approaches, algorithms, and processes used in environmental sciences. We will consider topics such as predicting fires using satellite data, analyzing strategies to improve conservation, and understanding the use of time series data for environmental purposes. Students will be taught to make predictions of migration patterns, temperatures, rising ocean levels, limitations in water sources, and crop growths.

courses.subject: CSS
courses.title: Introduction to Computational Social Science
courses.description: Overview of causal and statistical inference, data types/structure, and modeling/analytical approaches to social science data. Topics include models of social phenomena at different scales (cognition, behavior, learning, communication, language, game theory, markets, etc.) and analysis of different types of social data (social networks, text, GIS, timeseries, etc.). Emphasis is placed on the understanding of analytical and modeling methods, their applications and limitations. Open to CT75 majors only.

courses.subject: CSS
courses.title: Computational Social Science Technical Boot Camp
courses.description: This course provides practical experience with the technical skills underpinning computational social science. Topics may include calculus, linear algebra, probability, Unix/Linux, working in the terminal, file encoding, file system organization, Python, numpy, pandas, scikit, notebooks, matplotlib, code style, scraping, data storage, SQL, JSON, CSV/TSV, version control, git, spreadsheets, algorithms, basic data visualization, and machine learning basics. Open to CT75 majors only.

courses.subject: CSS
courses.title: Statistical Methods for Computational Social Science
courses.description: An introduction to the methods used by computational social scientists for data analysis, statistics, computing, inference, and machine learning, constituting the first part of a series of courses in CSS methods. This course covers research design, causal inference, data wrangling, visualization, probability, statistical inference, and statistical computing.

courses.subject: CSS
courses.title: Advanced Statistical Applications
courses.description: Use of advanced quantitative techniques in social science. Students will use social science data to complete small exercises and a major project.
courses.prereqText: graduate standing, CSS 204, POLI 204B, POLI 270, or PSYC 201A.

courses.subject: CSS
courses.title: Computational Social Science Research Seminar
courses.description: A weekly seminar series focused on selected topics in computational social science.

courses.subject: CSS
courses.title: Research in Computational Social Science
courses.description: Independent research under the supervision of individual faculty members.

courses.subject: CSS
courses.title: Teaching Apprentice
courses.description: Graduate students are required to enroll in a teaching assistantship course while supporting undergraduate courses.
